question: What substance is put into a vaccine to trigger the body's immune defense?
explanation: Great job! Vaccines carry harmless pieces of germs called antigens. This teaches your immune system what the real germ looks like without making you sick. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h1)

question: Years after getting a vaccine, why can your body fight off the same infection so much faster?

options.A: White blood cells permanently increase their normal physical size
options.B: The original vaccine stays active inside the bloodstream forever
options.C: Circulating antibiotics permanently block all future viruses
options.D: Immunological memory allows a rapid secondary response

explanation: You've got this! Your immune system has a great memory. It remembers past encounters and mounts a quick, powerful defense when the real germ shows up later. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h1)

question: Which type of vaccine contains a weakened form of a live germ?
explanation: Spot on! 'Live-attenuated' means a living germ has been weakened (attenuated) so it can safely spark a strong immune response. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h2)

question: Why do inactivated (killed) vaccines usually need booster doses compared to live vaccines?

options.A: They do not multiply in the body, so they trigger a weaker immune response.
options.B: They contain toxic chemicals that destroy early antibody production.
options.C: They target multiple diseases simultaneously instead of a single pathogen.
options.D: They dissolve too quickly inside the muscular tissue before antibodies form.

explanation: Makes total sense, right? Since dead germs cannot multiply inside you, your body often needs a few extra reminders (boosters) to build long-term protection. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h2)

question: On a Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM), what does it mean if the inner square becomes darker than the outer circle?

options.A: The vial is fresh and safe for immediate patient administration
options.B: The vaccine has been exposed to excessive heat and must be discarded
options.C: The vial has expired according to the printed calendar date
options.D: The vaccine has been frozen and lost its structural potency

explanation: Good to know for clinicals! VVMs change color when they soak up too much heat. If the inner square is darker than the circle, the vaccine has spoiled and shouldn't be used. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h3)

question: When giving the BCG vaccine to a newborn, which injection route and technique should you use?

options.A: Deep intramuscular injection at a 90-degree angle
options.B: Oral drops placed directly onto the tongue
options.C: Subcutaneous injection into the fatty thigh tissue
options.D: Intradermal injection forming a small skin bleb

explanation: You'll practice this a lot in clinic! BCG goes right into the top layer of skin (intradermal), which raises a nice little skin bleb. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h3)

question: In Nigeria's routine immunization schedule, which vaccines are given right at birth?

options.C: BCG, OPV 0, and Hepatitis B birth dose
options.D: Inactivated Polio Vaccine and Tetanus toxoid

explanation: Always remember the birth trio: BCG, oral polio zero (OPV 0), and the Hepatitis B birth dose are given before the baby leaves the maternity ward! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h4)

question: An 8-month-old baby comes to the clinic having missed their 14-week doses. What should you do?

options.A: Restart the entire immunization series from the very beginning
options.B: Continue the schedule from where they stopped using catch-up principles
options.C: Give only adult-strength boosters to make up for lost time
options.D: Wait until the child turns one year old before administering any new vaccines

explanation: No need to restart! Immunization schedules are cumulative. Just use catch-up principles to pick up right where they left off. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h4)

question: If an older child or teenager faints right after getting an injection, what is this usually classified as?
explanation: Needle fear is real! Fainting right after a shot is typically an anxiety-related reaction, not a bad reaction to the vaccine itself. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h5)

question: Why is it important for nurses to report both real vaccine reactions and random health events that happen after vaccination?

options.A: To prove that pharmaceutical manufacturing companies are always at fault for patient illness
options.B: To automatically trigger immediate free hospital admission for every sick child
options.C: To help health authorities investigate and determine the true root cause of the incident
options.D: To legally punish mothers who bring their children late for routine clinic appointments

explanation: Reporting helps public health experts look at the facts, figure out what really happened, and keep immunization safe for everyone. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h5)

question: What is the main difference between a vaccine contraindication and a precaution?

options.A: A contraindication allows live vaccines, while a precaution requires immediate quarantine.
options.B: A contraindication is a mild fever, while a precaution is always a permanent physical disability.
options.C: A contraindication means the vaccine is unsafe, while a precaution means it should be delayed or used with caution.
options.D: A contraindication only applies to adults, while a precaution applies exclusively to newborn infants.

explanation: Spot on! A contraindication means 'Stop, this is unsafe here,' while a precaution means 'Proceed with caution or wait a little bit.' [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h6)

question: A 10-week-old baby is brought for immunizations, but currently has a high fever and a bad cough. What should you do?

options.A: Refer the child straight to surgery for a diagnostic blood test
options.B: Defer the immunizations temporarily until the acute illness resolves
options.C: Administer all scheduled vaccines immediately regardless of the fever
options.D: Permanently ban the child from receiving any future vaccines

explanation: When a child is acutely sick with a high fever, it's wise to hold off (defer) the shots until they feel better so symptoms don't get confused. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h6)

question: How should you talk to a parent who is scared about vaccines because of community rumors?

options.A: Tell the parent that asking questions about modern medicine is illegal
options.B: Scold the parent publicly to discourage other community members from doubting
options.C: Listen respectfully, validate their concerns, and provide clear factual explanations
options.D: Ignore the questions entirely and administer the injections without speaking

explanation: As a nurse, patience is key. Listening without judgment and sharing gentle, honest facts builds trust way faster than arguing. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h7)

question: Who do families in local communities typically trust the most when it comes to health advice?
explanation: That's you! Nurses hold a special, trusted place in the community, making your health advice powerful for local families. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T16#GNS215_U6_T16_h7)
